D.; two recensions of his work are known through their Skt. adaptations (1) the Kashmir recension represented by Somadeva's Kathāsaritsāgara (See NCC. III. p. 136b) an. Kṣemendra's Bṛhatkathāmañjarī (See NCC. V. p. 168), an. (2) the so-called Nepal recension represented by the Bṛhatkathāślokasaṅgraha of Budhasvāmin. The Gaṅga King Durvinīta, contemporary of Bhāravi (7th Cent. A. D.) is said to have made a Skt. rendering of the work (Ind. Ant. 1913, p. 204; JRAS. 1913, p. 389 ff.). There is a Tamil version in the Peruṅkatai of Koṅguvel, edn. U. Swaminatha Iyer, Madras, 1924 (C. 2nd Cent. A. D.) an. a Persian version, see Lacote, Essai, p. 197 ff.
The Pkt. version of the story is found in Vāsudeva-hiṇḍī of Saṅghadāsa an. Dharmasena (See L. Alsdorf, BSOAS. VIII. p.. 320 ff).
Ref. to by Daṇḍin, Subandhu, Bāṇa; also by Jinasena (Ādipurāṇa), an. Somadeva (Yaśastilakacampū). On stories about Guṇāḍhya see also Jayaratha's Haracaritacintāmaṇi. Govardhana considers him a. incarnation of Vyāsa.
